### 🟢 Approval recommended The one-line resolver swap correctly applies the existing config precedence, matches the established doctor shared-resolver convention, and is fully covered by the new precedence tests. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR fixes `chroxy doctor`'s Port-availability check so it probes the port that `chroxy start` would actually bind, instead of only honoring an explicit CLI `--port` (or falling back to the hardcoded `8765`). The previous code (`const checkPort = port || 8765`) ignored both the `PORT` environment variable and a `port` entry in the config file, so `doctor` could report the wrong port as available/in-use. The fix routes the port through the shared `mergeConfig` resolver fed the already-parsed config file, bringing the Port check into line with how `doctor` already resolves providers and the binary-provenance gate (shared-resolver / "doctor parity" convention). **Changes:** - Resolve the doctor Port check via `mergeConfig({ fileConfig: parsedConfig, cliOverrides: { port }, defaults: { port: 8765 } })`, giving precedence CLI → `PORT` → config file → `8765`. - Update the `options.port` JSDoc to document the new override/fallback order. - Add `doctor-port.test.js`, which exercises `runDoctorChecks` end-to-end (mocking only the `net` socket boundary and binary resolution) across all precedence tiers plus the first-run no-config case. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `packages/​server/​src/​doctor.js` | Replaces `port \|\| 8765` with a `mergeConfig`-resolved port and updates the JSDoc, matching the precedence `chroxy start` uses. | | `packages/​server/​tests/​doctor-port.test.js` | New test covering CLI/`PORT`/config/default precedence and first-run behavior by mocking only the socket boundary and binary resolver. | I confirmed: `mergeConfig` maps `port`→`PORT` and parses it to a number (`config.js:1729,1837-1840`); the default `8765` matches `chroxy start` (`cli/shared.js:271-281`); `configFile()`/`configDir()` re-read `CHROXY_CONFIG_DIR` per call so the test env overrides are honored; the test's `binaryProvenanceMode`/`binarySignatureGate` option names match the `runDoctorChecks` destructure; and the `net` mock aligns with `checkPortAvailable`'s `createServer`/`listen(port, '127.0.0.1')` usage. No issues found.
Review effort: Balanced
